* Empirical studies link CO2 emissions, economic growth, energy demand.
- Cross-country regressions report inverted-U EKC; linear patterns dominate low-income panels.
- Time-series VARs identify bidirectional causality; structural breaks alter EKC estimates.

* Theoretical models embed environmental externalities, technological change, capital accumulation.
- Endogenous-growth frameworks show emissions rise, subsequently clean technology expands.
- Environmental Kuznets Curve theory requires income thresholds, policy instruments, trade openness.

* Methodological debates emphasize endogeneity, unit roots, nonstationarity.
- Panel-data cointegration tests reject weak exogeneity; system-GMM improves finite-sample inference.
- Spatial-econometric models reveal emission leakage, regional heterogeneity, scale effects.

* Policy implications suggest carbon pricing, renewable subsidies, green innovation.
- Tax simulations estimate modest welfare losses, substantial decarbonization, technology diffusion.
- Trade-policy analyses show carbon-border adjustments, compliance costs, industrial relocation.
